# 01 — Data audit: legacy vector shorelines (B) and risk polygons (C)

*Generated by `make audit` (`src/aparri/audit.py`) — numbers are computed, not typed. Read-only: nothing in `data/raw/` was changed. All lengths/areas are in EPSG:32651 (metres). Verdicts: **CONFIRMED / REFUTED / INCONCLUSIVE** about the first-pass hypotheses in CLAUDE.md §4. Terms: **EPR** (End Point Rate) = shoreline movement between the first and last date divided by the years between them, m/yr, negative = landward = erosion. **NSM** (Net Shoreline Movement) = that movement in metres.*

## Executive summary (≤10 lines)

1. **Risk polygons (C): do not cite.** Only 3 EPR values exist (0.8571, 2.586, 5.726); `Risk_Code` and `label` are the constant 1 in all 124 rows.
2. **Two different things are mixed in one layer.** 117 polygons (105.6 ha) are vectorised 850 m² raster cells (area = `count` × 0.0850 ha; 100 % of vertices on the 30 m pixel lattice). The other 7 polygons (all the 2.59 "Medium" and both "High" ones, 63.2 ha) have few vertices (median 14), **0 % on the lattice**, and cover 0.5–3.6 km each: they look **hand-drawn**.
3. **48 polygons break the thesis rule itself** ("Medium" but EPR = 0.857 < 2) and **every EPR is positive**, i.e. *accretion* under the thesis sign convention.
4. **They cannot be reproduced from the Earth Engine rasters**: under the "High" polygons the raster has *no* High pixel (EPR between -3.09 and 0.86 m/yr); 20.7 ha lie outside the raster extent.
5. **Shoreline lines (B): partly usable as context, not as measurements.** Years have 3–6 unjoined fragments, vertex spacing from 85 to 255 m, the 2010 coast is digitised **twice** in one stretch (56.7 km listed, only ≈ 39.1 km unique), and one feature has the year "Hig".
6. **Thesis text vs data:** the 2 hand-drawn High polygons do lie at Bulala Sur (8.3 ha) and Bulala Norte (12.0 ha), as the thesis says, but they also put 15.4 ha of High in **Linao** (thesis: Low) and no Medium in Bulala Norte (thesis: Medium); the Earth Engine raster shows **no High on the Bulala coast at all** (§6).
7. **No demonstrated link** between Fig. 4.1/4.2, the lines, the polygons and the rasters: 7 of 9 local layer links in the QGIS project are broken and no print layout locks its layer set (§7).
8. **Verdict — can we cite the legacy numbers? Risk polygons: NO. Shoreline lines: PARTLY** (as an unverified visual reference and as a candidate input to the rebuild, after cleaning; never as published rates).

---

## 1. Risk-layer attribute audit — CONFIRMED

**Method.** Read `Aparri_MultiTemporal_Erosion_Risk_1990_2025.shp` (byte-identical to `Aparri Risk Ana.shp`, same sha256), tabulate labels, EPR values, `count`, geometry; compute areas in EPSG:32651.

| Fact | Result |
|---|---|
| Polygons / geometry types | 124 / {'Polygon': 102, 'MultiPolygon': 22} (3 invalid geometries, repaired in memory only) |
| Label spellings in the `.shp` | Hig, LOW, Med — the `.dbf` field `Risk_Level` is **C(3)**: a 3-character text field, so "High"→"Hig" and "Medium"→"Med" were **truncated on export**. (`EPR Results.xlsx` has the un-truncated "High".) |
| Distinct EPR values | 3: [0.857143, 2.5864, 5.72642] (the Earth Engine EPR raster has 128 distinct values) |
| `Risk_Code` / `label` | constant [1] / [1] — carry no information |
| NaN rows | 0 |

Polygons and area per label:

| Risk_Level | polygons | area_ha | pixels_in_count |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hig | 2 | 35.70 | 2 |
| LOW | 69 | 84.60 | 996 |
| Med | 53 | 48.49 | 254 |

Crosstab label × EPR (count of polygons):

| Risk_Level | 0.857143 | 2.5864 | 5.72642 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hig | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| LOW | 69 | 0 | 0 |
| Med | 48 | 5 | 0 |

**What is `count`?** For 117 polygons the ratio *area ÷ count* is **0.0849 ha ± 0.00000**, equal to the area of one Landsat-grid pixel at this latitude (0.0850 ha; 28.5 m × 29.8 m). So for those polygons `count` **is a pixel count**. For the remaining 7 polygons it is not (area ÷ count = 1.5–22.7 ha):

| Risk_Level | EPR_90_25 | pixel_type | polygons | area_ha | count | median_vertices | min_ha | max_ha |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hig | 5.73 | False | 2 | 35.70 | 2 | 18.00 | 13.00 | 22.71 |
| Med | 2.59 | False | 5 | 27.51 | 7 | 11.00 | 1.52 | 9.27 |

## 2. Threshold consistency (Table 3.1) — CONFIRMED

**Method.** Apply Low < 2, Medium 2–5, High > 5 m/yr to each polygon's own EPR (read as an erosion magnitude) and compare with its label.

* **48 of 124 polygons violate the rule**:

| Risk_Level | polygons | area_ha |
|---|---|---|
| Med | 48 | 20.98 |

* All EPR values are **positive** (True); the thesis states "negative = erosion", so read literally the layer describes *accretion*. Reading them as magnitudes (the only reading that gives a risk map) means the sign was dropped without a record.
* The two "High" polygons carry EPR 5.726 and the five "Medium (2.59)" polygons carry 2.586: they satisfy the rule, but these are exactly the hand-drawn polygons of §3.

## 3. Pixel-size hypothesis and reproduction from the rasters — CONFIRMED

**Method.** (i) Is 0.857143 = 30/35? (ii) Do vertices lie on the 30 m lattice of the Earth Engine rasters (origin 121.57979, 18.39004; cell 0.00026949°)? (iii) Rasterise the polygons onto the Earth Engine risk raster and cross-tabulate.

* 30/35 = 0.857143 → **0.857143 is exactly one 30 m pixel of change over 35 years.** It is a class constant for the smallest possible change, not a measured mean. 2.5864 × 35 = 90.52 m and 5.72642 × 35 = 200.4 m are **not** multiples of 30 m: they cannot come from the pixel-distance method — **REFUTED** for those two values.
* Vertex-on-lattice test (tolerance 2 % of a cell; chance level ≈ 4 %):

| Layer / subset | vertices | on lattice (x) | on lattice (y) | both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Risk polygons, all | 1360 | 92.3% | 91.9% | 91.6% |
| …pixel-type polygons (117) | 1246 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% |
| …other polygons (7) | 114 | 7.9% | 3.5% | 0.0% |
| Shoreline lines (B) | 1758 | 3.6% | 3.9% | 0.1% |

  → the 117 pixel-type polygons are **vectorised raster cells on the same lattice as our rasters**; the 7 others and **all shoreline lines were not made from a raster** (CONFIRMED).
* Reproduction test — pixels of the Earth Engine **risk raster** (rows = polygon label, columns = raster class 1 Low / 2 Medium / 3 High):

| index | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| LOW | 605 | 319 | 72 |
| Med | 450 | 10 | 2 |
| Hig | 227 | 32 | 0 |

  Raster totals: Low 115,708 · Medium 387 · High 88. Of the raster's 88 High pixels, only 74 lie in any polygon and those fall mostly in *Low* polygons.
  EPR values of the raster under the polygons: **High polygons** n=259, min -3.09, median 0.00, max 0.86 m/yr; **Medium polygons** min -10.00, median 0.00; **Low polygons** min -82.0, median -1.71.
  Only 61% of the pixels under *Low* polygons are Low in the raster, and **no** pixel under a *High* polygon is High.
* Extent: 20.7 ha of polygon area lies outside the raster footprint (x 121.580–121.720, y 18.330–18.390), so a full reproduction is impossible even in principle.

**Verdict: the polygons cannot be reproduced from the Earth Engine rasters.** Their origin is some other run (or manual work) that was never supplied.

## 4. Shoreline-layer audit

**Method.** Reproject to EPSG:32651; per feature compute length, vertices, self-crossing (`is_simple`), duplicate vertices, endpoint gaps to the nearest other fragment of the same year and the share that runs within 15 m of another fragment of the same year.

* The layer's year column is literally named **"1990"** (type C(80)) and `id` is empty in all rows → the table was imported with its first data row used as the header.

| year_raw | features | total_km | vertices | non_simple_features | dup_vertices | max_overlap_frac | mean_vertex_spacing_m | unique_km | duplicated_km |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1990 | 3 | 35.41 | 142 | 1 | 0 | 0.00 | 254.75 | 35.35 | 0.06 |
| 2000 | 3 | 41.08 | 328 | 1 | 3 | 0.00 | 126.39 | 41.06 | 0.02 |
| 2010 | 4 | 56.72 | 670 | 0 | 2 | 0.59 | 85.17 | 39.11 | 17.62 |
| 2020 | 3 | 35.52 | 337 | 0 | 4 | 0.16 | 106.36 | 34.88 | 0.65 |
| 2025 | 6 | 40.83 | 262 | 1 | 3 | 0.01 | 159.51 | 40.70 | 0.14 |
| Hig | 1 | 3.14 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 0.00 | 174.61 | 3.14 | 0.00 |

* **2010 is 56.7 km because part of the coast was digitised twice.** Features 3, 10 and 11 overlap each other for up to 59% of their length; counting each stretch once (duplicates digitised up to 60 m apart) gives ≈ **39.1 km** (duplicated ≈ 17.6 km). **CONFIRMED** as the reason for the unusual total.
* Other years: 1990 35.4 km, 2020 35.5 km differ from 2000/2025 (≈ 41 km) because fragments are missing, not because the coast changed: see the gaps below.
* Vertex density differs 5-fold between years (mean spacing 85–255 m; the 1990 SE open coast is 33 vertices over 18.5 km = 577 m!). Lines digitised at such different detail are **not comparable** at the metre level that a 0.86 m/yr rate needs.
* Self-crossing features (loops): 0, 6, 17 (fid) — river-mouth loops.

Fragments (fid = row number in the shapefile):

| fid | year_raw | length_km | n_vertices | mean_vertex_spacing_m | is_simple | dup_vertices | gap_start_m | gap_end_m | overlap_with_same_year_frac |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1990 | 11.10 | 70 | 160.93 | False | 0 | 4,632.92 | 657.16 | 0.00 |
| 1 | 1990 | 5.83 | 39 | 153.40 | True | 0 | 657.16 | 1,660.13 | 0.00 |
| 2 | 1990 | 18.48 | 33 | 577.39 | True | 0 | 12,893.62 | 1,660.13 | 0.00 |
| 5 | 2000 | 19.82 | 124 | 161.11 | True | 2 | 13,047.08 | 1,891.03 | 0.00 |
| 6 | 2000 | 17.16 | 160 | 107.92 | False | 1 | 1,891.03 | 3,367.25 | 0.00 |
| 7 | 2000 | 4.10 | 44 | 95.40 | True | 0 | 4,551.43 | 3,367.25 | 0.00 |
| 3 | 2010 | 18.70 | 309 | 60.73 | True | 0 | 25.58 | 15.74 | 0.58 |
| 4 | 2010 | 19.74 | 278 | 71.26 | True | 2 | 1,675.92 | 13,050.14 | 0.00 |
| 10 | 2010 | 7.17 | 38 | 193.78 | True | 0 | 15.74 | 1,263.91 | 0.59 |
| 11 | 2010 | 11.11 | 45 | 252.52 | True | 0 | 1,263.91 | 25.58 | 0.58 |
| 8 | 2020 | 19.45 | 233 | 83.86 | True | 4 | 12,929.71 | 2,172.62 | 0.01 |
| 9 | 2020 | 1.66 | 19 | 92.06 | True | 0 | 2,171.24 | 2,175.22 | 0.16 |
| 12 | 2020 | 14.41 | 85 | 171.56 | True | 0 | 2,171.24 | 9,038.51 | 0.00 |
| 13 | 2025 | 4.14 | 7 | 689.64 | True | 0 | 3,513.75 | 0.48 | 0.00 |
| 14 | 2025 | 10.40 | 135 | 77.58 | True | 0 | 0.48 | 1,366.22 | 0.00 |
| 15 | 2025 | 4.42 | 36 | 126.16 | True | 0 | 2,003.09 | 524.27 | 0.01 |

| 19 | Hig | 3.14 | 19 | 174.61 | True | 0 |  |  | 0.00 |

* **Gaps.** Between fragments of the same year the endpoint gaps are up to 13.1 km (e.g. 1990 fid 2 starts 12.9 km from the nearest other 1990 fragment): the gaps coincide with the Cagayan River mouth, which was left open in every year. A "continuous shoreline" does not exist in any year.
* **Coverage / common extent.** Projecting every vertex on the NW→SE axis of the coast, every year covers 0.0–21.8 km; the common extent of the five years is 0.04–21.75 km, i.e. essentially the whole 21.8 km — **extent is not the problem**; fragment gaps and the duplicated 2010 stretch are.

### The feature labelled "Hig"

Feature 19 (3.1 km, x≈351,6–351,7 E, y≈2,032,3 N, Bulala Norte–Linao coast) has the text "Hig" in the year column — the same truncation word as the risk layer, so it was probably pasted from it. **Its true year is not assigned here.** Evidence for a human to weigh:

| year_raw | median_dist_to_hig_m | p95_dist_m | share_hig_within_30m | length_of_year_inside_hig_zone_m |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1990 | 81.65 | 246.99 | 0.16 | 1,053.49 |
| 2000 | 124.26 | 212.68 | 0.05 | 542.54 |
| 2010 | 70.35 | 113.02 | 0.05 | 3,321.48 |
| 2020 | 42.98 | 143.25 | 0.26 | 1,754.85 |
| 2025 | 65.85 | 138.18 | 0.37 | 1,291.80 |

Reading: a year that has *no* line near this stretch is a candidate (least length inside the 100 m zone: **2000**, then 1990); the year whose lines run closest to it (median distance) is **2020**. The two criteria disagree, so the answer is **INCONCLUSIVE** — the students must tell us or the feature stays excluded (Phase 3A rule).

## 6. Thesis text vs legacy data — CONFIRMED contradictions

Chapter IV says: *High* in Bulala Sur and Bulala Norte; *Medium* in Bulala Norte, Punta, San Antonio, Maura, Dodan, Paddaya; *Low* in Linao. Area (ha) by class, nearest-within-tolerance attribution:

| brg | Low | Medium | High |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linao | 27.26 | 9.27 | 15.40 |
| Maura | 0.32 | 18.34 | 0.00 |
| Punta | 0.17 | 3.73 | 0.00 |
| San Antonio | 0.00 | 2.74 | 0.00 |
| Bulala Sur | 0.00 | 0.00 | 8.27 |
| Bulala Norte | 0.00 | 0.00 | 12.04 |
| Dodan | 0.00 | 5.35 | 0.00 |
| Paddaya | 0.00 | 9.30 | 0.00 |
| (no barangay within tolerance) | 56.85 | 0.00 | 0.00 |

Contradictions found:

* Thesis says Medium risk occurs in Bulala Norte, but the legacy layer has 0.00 ha of Medium attributed to Bulala Norte.
* The legacy layer puts 15.4 ha of High risk in Linao; the thesis does not list High risk there.
* The legacy layer puts 9.3 ha of Medium risk in Linao; the thesis does not list it.

(The Earth Engine barangay table is audited in `docs/01b_gee_audit.md`; the Earth Engine rasters give only ≈ 1.4 ha of High inside the eight official polygons — Linao 1.27 ha, Maura 0.17 ha — and **none in Bulala Sur or Bulala Norte**.)

## 7. QGIS-project forensics

* QGIS 3.44.11-Solothurn, saved **2026-10-01T10:22:36** by "Admin", project CRS **EPSG:3857** (not metric-safe). The manuscript is dated April 2026, so the project is *newer* than the figures printed in it.
* Visibility presets: none; processing history stored: False → **no record of how any layer was produced.**

| layer | type | crs | is_local_file | found_on_disk | renderer_field |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aparri Barangays | vector | EPSG:4326 | True | True |  |
| Aparri_Brgy_Study | vector | EPSG:4326 | True | True |  |
| Risk | vector | EPSG:4326 | True | False | Risk_Level |
| Aparri_Shoreline_1990 | raster | EPSG:4326 | True | False |  |
| Aparri_Shoreline_2000 | raster | EPSG:4326 | True | False |  |
| Aparri_Shoreline_2010 | raster | EPSG:4326 | True | False |  |
| Aparri_Shoreline_2020 | raster | EPSG:4326 | True | False |  |
| Aparri_Shoreline_2025 | raster | EPSG:4326 | True | False |  |
| ESRI OSM Standard | vector-tile | EPSG:3857 | False | None |  |
| Esri Light Gray | raster | EPSG:3857 | False | None |  |
| Google Satellite | raster | EPSG:3857 | False | None |  |
| Shoreline Changes 1990-2025 | vector | EPSG:4326 | True | False | 1990 |

* 7 of 9 local sources are **broken** (point to `../../../Downloads/...`): the rasters and the risk shapefile (named `Risk`), and `Shoreline Changes 1990-2025.shp` — a file that was never supplied (the supplied one is `Shoreline Changes.shp`). Two different Earth Engine export folders appear in the paths (`Final_Aparri_Erosion_Assessment`, `Aparri_Erosion_Assessment-20260917T050811Z-1-001`): **at least two export runs exist**.

| layout | title | map_items | layer_set_locked | follows_preset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Layout 1 | Multi-Temporal Shoreline Change Map | 1 | False | False |
| Layout 2 | Erosion Risk Map | 1 | False | False |
| Layout 3 | Multi-Temporal Shoreline Change Map | 1 | False | False |
| Layout 4 | Coastal Erosion Risk Map of Selected Coastal Barangays in Aparri, Cagayan | 1 | False | False |

* Figure ↔ layer: Layout 4's title ("Coastal Erosion Risk Map of Selected Coastal Barangays in Aparri…") matches thesis **Fig. 4.2**; the thesis Fig. 4.1 title ("Multi-Temporal Shoreline Change Map of Selected Coastal Barangays…") matches **no saved layout exactly** (Layouts 1 and 3 have a shorter title). `layer_set_locked = False` for every map item: a layout shows whatever is ticked in the project *at export time*, so the project cannot prove which layer made which figure. The exported draft maps (`Erosion Risk Map.jpeg`, `Multi Temporal Risk.jpeg`) show only green cells.
* **Is there any demonstrated link between the lines (B), the polygons (C) and the rasters (A)?** Only a weak one: B and C have almost the same bounding box (x 121.563–121.755, y 18.319–18.392), larger than the rasters', suggesting the same working AOI; and 117 polygons sit on the rasters' pixel lattice. Nothing shows B was derived from A or C from A. **INCONCLUSIVE → treat as unlinked.**

## 8. Diagnostic maps

`outputs/maps/audit_risk_by_label.png` (polygons by label; hand-drawn ones outlined), `audit_shoreline_fragments_by_year.png` (fragments and endpoints per year), `audit_river_mouth_zoom.png` (same, river-mouth area), `audit_barangay_edges.png` (coast vs barangay edges). Tables: `outputs/tables/audit_*.csv`.

## What this means for the rebuild

* Use none of the legacy **numbers**. The legacy **lines** can seed the rebuilt analysis only after cleaning (Phase 3A) and only if the students can tell us how they were made; they are compared with an independent raster-derived set in Phase 3B.
* Questions the data cannot answer (CLAUDE.md §6 "Open questions"): who drew the 7 large polygons and the 20 lines; the true year of the "Hig" feature; why 2010 has a duplicated stretch; which export run feeds Fig. 4.2.
